name: Typesense
model: JSON documents in typed collections; typo-tolerant instant search, facets, filters, vector and hybrid search over a REST API
engine_note: Whole search index held in RAM; a copy of the raw documents kept on disk (RocksDB) and replayed to rebuild the index on start
consistency: Single-document writes; no multi-document transactions. A cluster uses Raft: writes go through the leader and are replicated to every node; reads are served by whichever node gets them, and the docs do not promise those are up to date.
scaling: No sharding: every node holds the whole dataset (3 or 5 node Raft cluster for availability), so dataset size is capped by one node's RAM; scale reads by adding nodes or grow the machine.
reach: Reach for it for search-as-you-type over a catalogue or help centre that fits in one machine's RAM, when you want simple ops and good typo tolerance out of the box.
avoid: Avoid when the index will not fit in RAM on one node, or you need log-scale analytics or the source of truth for your data.
escape: Postgres LIKE and full-text search lack instant, typo-tolerant, faceted search UX.
chat: A search-as-you-type index over chat titles and message snippets for one user's history.
notes: Docs quotes: 'it stores the entire search index in-memory and a copy of the raw data on disk'; 'each node holds the entire replicated copy of your dataset and can handle searches independently'; 'Typesense uses the Raft consensus algorithm'. The RocksDB name for the on-disk store comes from the source tree, not the docs page read (unconfirmed from docs). Follower read staleness not documented: stated as 'not promised'. No Jepsen analysis. v30.2 and v29.1 were released the same day (2026-04-19); 30.2 is the newest.
